mainEntity.name: What is an AC to DC converter?

acceptedAnswer.text: A circuit or power-supply assembly that accepts alternating current and provides a DC output. A rectifier establishes one-way current; filtering, regulation, isolation and protection may be additional stages.

mainEntity.name: How do you convert AC voltage to DC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Select a suitable rectifier, account for its conducting diode path and output waveform, then consider filtering and regulation for the load. Use a correctly rated isolated supply for practical mains-powered equipment.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a rectifier and a complete converter?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rectifier can produce pulsating DC. A complete regulated converter may also provide isolation, energy storage, voltage or current control and protection. The words are sometimes used loosely; inspect the actual stages.

There is no universal best topology. Source winding, load power, available headroom, ripple, isolation and thermal constraints determine the choice. A bridge is common for single-phase supplies but is not loss-free.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate DC output voltage?

acceptedAnswer.text: First decide whether you need an unfiltered waveform average, a filtered estimate or a regulated setpoint. RMS, peak, average and ripple valley answer different questions. The calculator separates these models.

mainEntity.name: How do you convert 220 V AC to 12 V DC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use an appropriately rated, isolated AC-to-DC supply specified for the input and load. Rectifying 220 V RMS directly produces a crest near 311 V before losses, not 12 V. This site does not provide exposed-mains construction instructions.

mainEntity.name: What does the filter capacitor do?

acceptedAnswer.text: It supplies load current between charging peaks, reducing voltage variation. A heavier load or smaller capacitance generally increases ripple. It does not create regulated voltage or guarantee a safe output.
Residual variation around the DC component. Peak-to-peak ripple is highest minus lowest voltage; RMS ripple factor is AC-component RMS divided by average DC. These are different measures.

mainEntity.name: How do half-wave and full-wave rectification differ?

acceptedAnswer.text: Half-wave uses one half-cycle and has pulse frequency f. Full-wave uses both halves and has pulse frequency 2f for a single-phase sine input. Their complete-cycle averages and filter discharge intervals differ.

Input waveform and RMS convention, rectifier topology, diode loss, source impedance, filter size, load, line variation and regulator behavior. A voltage label alone does not establish available current.

mainEntity.name: How are RMS and peak voltage related?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a sine wave, Vpeak = √2 Vrms. This relationship does not apply unchanged to square waves or arbitrary distorted signals. Peak-to-peak sine voltage is twice its peak amplitude.

It depends on the complete architecture and operating point. Measure real input watts and output watts for whole-supply efficiency. A diode-loss estimate or regulator-stage efficiency is not the same quantity.
